blocks.text: Why Slack matters for your creative workflow

For a copywriter, your Mac is your studio. Slack often acts as the main hub where briefs arrive, feedback is shared, and deadlines are set. When you manage Slack well, you protect your creative time. When you let it run wild, it fragments your day into small, unproductive chunks. You need to treat Slack as a tool you control, not a radio that plays constantly.
Stop using your mouse for navigation. Every second you spend clicking is a second away from your document. Use these shortcuts to move faster on macOS.

items: Command + K: The Quick Switcher. Jump to any channel or direct message.
Command + /: Opens the full list of keyboard shortcuts.
Shift + Enter: Create a new line in your message without sending it.
Command + B: Bold your selected text.
Command + I: Italicize your selected text.
Command + ,: Open your Slack preferences immediately.

blocks.text: Managing notifications to protect deep work

Marketing copy requires deep focus. Constant Slack pings are the enemy of good writing. Use the built-in notification schedules to batch your communication. Open your preferences with Command + , and navigate to the Notifications tab. Set a schedule that only allows alerts during your non-writing hours. If you need a break, use the profile menu to pause notifications for a set time.

Copywriters often work across multiple client workspaces. Keep your sidebar clean. Star your most active project channels to keep them at the top. Use the Unreads view to see only what you have missed. If a channel becomes too noisy, mute it. You can always check in on it later without being interrupted by every single message.

If you find yourself searching for the same files repeatedly, pin them to the channel. Use the three dots menu on any message to pin it. This keeps essential briefs or style guides visible for everyone in the channel.

blocks.text: Slack can sometimes feel sluggish, especially on older hardware or after long sessions. If the app feels slow, go to Help > Troubleshooting > Clear Cache and Restart. This usually fixes performance issues. Ensure you are running the latest version of macOS, at least Sonoma or newer, to maintain compatibility with the latest Slack updates.

faq.question: How do I find a specific message in Slack?
faq.answer: Use Command + G to open the general search bar. You can use modifiers like from:@username or in:#channel to narrow down your results quickly.

faq.question: Can I use voice to dictate messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. Hold the fn key on your Mac keyboard to use system-wide dictation. Lazur also allows you to dictate clean, formatted text directly into your cursor position in any app.

faq.question: Does Slack work on all Mac versions?
faq.answer: Slack requires macOS 14 (Sonoma) or above for the latest supported versions. It is updated twice a year, in May and November.
